name: NeuralPath Pro VectorStrike Pilot-Rated Neural Link
description:
The NeuralPath Pro VectorStrike is a Tier 4 pilot-rated vehicle neural link engineered for high-performance aerospace and ground assault vehicle operators who demand sub-millisecond neural-to-control latency in extreme operational environments. The core architecture centers on NeuralPath Pro's proprietary VectorSync neural bus, which establishes a bidirectional 6.4 Tbps data channel between the operator's motor cortex and a vehicle's primary flight or drive control system, eliminating the mechanical and electronic lag inherent in conventional interface methods. The VectorStrike's spatial awareness module fuses vehicle sensor arrays directly into the pilot's proprioceptive sense, allowing the operator to perceive the vehicle's hull, weapon systems, and environmental data as a seamless extension of their own body schema. An integrated G-force compensation predictor anticipates maneuver stress loads up to 180ms ahead of execution, automatically modulating neural signal intensity to prevent pilot incapacitation during extreme vector changes. The device requires four cortical anchor points and a dedicated spinal relay node implanted at the C3-C4 vertebral level for full vehicle embodiment capability.

In GLMZ's aerospace and armored vehicle communities, the VectorStrike has cultivated an almost mythological reputation. Pilots who have undergone full VectorStrike integration describe flying or driving as 'becoming the machine'—a phenomenological shift that many report they can never fully reverse even after the device is powered down. The GLMZ Defense Contracting Authority certifies the VectorStrike for use in seven distinct vehicle classifications, and NeuralPath Pro's exclusive supply contract with two major defense fleets has made the device the de facto standard for front-line vehicle operators. A small but vocal community of civilian racing enthusiasts have obtained VectorStrike units through gray-market channels, pushing the hardware into recreational contexts it was never designed to survive.

story_hooks: A decorated VectorStrike pilot has been reported AWOL—but surveillance footage shows their assigned assault craft executing precise combat maneuvers autonomously; someone or something is still inside the neural link.

A gray-market VectorStrike unit surfaces with an undocumented firmware layer that records and transmits full embodiment neural experiences to an unknown recipient—someone is collecting what it feels like to be a weapon.
